newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Central Bank not considering devaluation.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Central Bank not considering devaluation.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank said it was not considering a currency devaluation and stressed there was no pressure on local currency markets.
"We are in no way considering a currency devaluation. We already said so earlier this week," a Central Bank spokeswoman said in response to a Reuter question.
"We aren't seeing any pressure on the currency," the spokeswoman said.
At midday, Brazil's currency was essentially unchanged at 1.0811 reais in the commercial foreign exchange market, down 0.01 percent on the day.
There has been little movement in the real despite the storm of volatility that gripped Brazil's bolsa early this week.
Dealers said local currency markets were trading calmly with robust dollar inflows.
So far this month, net capital flows showed a surplus of $1.99 billion in the commercial foreign exchange market.
